name: Roberto Gonzalez Barrera
current_role: Deceased (died 25 Aug 2012, Houston, Texas); was chairman of Gruma and lifetime honorary chairman of Grupo Financiero Banorte
notes: Died 25 August 2012 aged 81. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Gonz%C3%A1lez_Barrera ; https://expansion.mx/negocios/2012/08/25/fallece-roberto-gonzalez-barrera . Son Juan Antonio Gonzalez Moreno now leads Gruma.

name: Mario Brescia Cafferata
current_role: Deceased (died 16 May 2013, Lima); was co-chairman of Grupo Breca and chairman of BBVA Continental
notes: Died May 2013. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Brescia_Cafferata ; https://www.mch.cl/fallece-empresario-peruano-mario-brescia-presidente-del-holding-breca-dueno-de-cemento-melon-y-pinturas-tricolor/ . Grupo Breca is now run by the next generation of the Brescia family.

name: Paolo Zegna
current_role: Non-executive director, Ermenegildo Zegna N.V.; vice-chairman of family holding Monterubello; chairman of Lanificio Ermenegildo Zegna e Figli
profile: Third-generation member of the Zegna family (born Turin 1956, economics degree from Geneva). He was co-CEO of the group in 1998-2006 and chairman from 2006 until the 2021 NYSE listing, and now sits on the board as a non-executive director. His cousin Gildo is executive chairman. He also chairs the historic Trivero wool mill.
interesting_fact: He served as president of Sistema Moda Italia, Italy's textile and apparel industry association. He has also been vice-president of the Altagamma Foundation and sits on the council of Euratex, the European textile association.
deep_cut_fact: He chairs Achill Land Pty Ltd, the company behind Zegna's 60%-owned Achill merino sheep farm east of Armidale, New South Wales. Zegna bought into the farm in 2014 to secure its own fine-wool supply. Sixth-generation grower Charlie Coventry kept the other 40%.
notes: The source of wealth matches (Zegna). No personal social accounts found. The best route is the group's corporate press office, which is run by Paola Durante, Chief of External Relations.

name: Chen Jiancheng
current_role: Founder and group chairman, Wolong Holding Group (Shangyu, Zhejiang)
profile: Founder of Wolong Group (born Shangyu 1959), a global maker of electric motors, generators and drive controls with interests in renewables. Its listed units include Wolong Electric Drive (600580.SH), Wolong New Energy and Brook Crompton. His daughter Chen Yanni is chairman and CEO of Wolong Holding, and his son-in-law Pang Xinyuan chairs Wolong Electric Drive.
interesting_fact: He was named China's EY World Entrepreneur Of The Year in 2019. His stated strategy is 'European technology, Chinese cost, global market', which he built through acquisitions such as Austria's ATB motors.
deep_cut_fact: Wolong began in 1984, when Chen and five partners pooled just over 50,000 yuan. They set up the Shangyu Multi-Speed Micro Motor Factory in a rented, run-down workshop at the foot of Wolong Mountain in Haobi township, which gave the company its name.
notes: Day-to-day leadership has passed to his daughter Chen Yanni (Wolong Holding) and son-in-law Pang Xinyuan (Wolong Electric Drive). Wolong is relevant to energy and storage topics: it has a Wolong Energy Storage unit and is pursuing a Hong Kong listing of Wolong Electric Drive. The IR email belongs to the listed company's board-secretary office.

name: Elisabeth Douglas
current_role: Swedish countess, landowner and investor; Douglas-family shareholder in Investment AB Latour (her sons Carl and Eric sit on Latour's board)
profile: Elisabeth Douglas (née von Essen, born 1941) is the widow of Count Gustaf Douglas, who founded Investment AB Latour in 1984 and died in 2023. Latour holds a large stake in Assa Abloy and owns industrial companies. The family still controls it, and she has served on the boards of Latour, Boxholms Skogar and Wasatornet.
interesting_fact: Her husband Gustaf turned a struggling security firm into Investment AB Latour, the vehicle behind Securitas and Assa Abloy. In 2013 he also bought the Treskilling Yellow, the world's only known example of Sweden's famous 1855 stamp.
deep_cut_fact: She is the granddaughter of bank director Henric Tamm and graduated from Stockholm's Whitlockska samskolan in 1961. With her sons, she co-owns the historic Rydboholm estate in Uppland, which she took over from her father, Baron Eric von Essen.
notes: Very private, with no public profile or social media. She is not on Latour's current board (checked latour.se, Nov 2026); her sons Carl and Eric Douglas are. The only realistic route is via Investment AB Latour or the family holding companies. No published email found.

name: Zbigniew Juroszek
current_role: Founder, main shareholder and President of the Management Board, ATAL S.A. (Cieszyn, Poland)
profile: Polish entrepreneur from Cieszyn. He started Atal in 1990 supplying clothing makers, moved into property in the late 1990s and built his first homes in 2003. Atal is now a Warsaw-listed developer active in Poland's major cities. He also founded the bookmaker STS, now run by his son Mateusz.
interesting_fact: He founded STS (Star-Typ Sport), which grew into Poland's largest bookmaker with roughly half the country's betting market. The family became sole owners in 2012 when its British partner Stanleybet withdrew.
deep_cut_fact: His first business was supplying fabrics to clothing manufacturers, and the textile roots survive: the family still runs Atal Textil, a wholesale fabric trader, alongside the property empire.
notes: He gives occasional interviews to Polish business media (Forbes Polska, Biznesradar) and has been a listed speaker at the European Economic Congress in Katowice in 2025 and 2026. The best route is via ATAL investor relations. He tends to appear publicly together with his son Mateusz, CEO of STS.

name: Jiang Xueying
current_role: Co-controlling shareholder (with husband Ling Shisheng) of Hangzhou AllTest Biotech (安旭生物, SSE STAR 688075)
profile: Jiang Xueying (姜学英) and her husband Ling Shisheng, the chairman and general manager, control Hangzhou AllTest Biotech, a maker of in-vitro diagnostics and rapid tests founded in 2008. Together they hold about 60%. Their wealth peaked on Hurun's 2022 lists during the Covid-19 testing boom.
interesting_fact: AllTest is an export-focused maker of rapid diagnostic tests (drugs of abuse, infectious disease, fertility and similar) and is listed on Shanghai's STAR Market. In filings, Jiang is named only as a shareholder, while her husband runs the company.
notes: Hurun's 'Assuro Tech' corresponds to 安旭生物 (AllTest); filings confirm she and Ling Shisheng are a married couple and the company's controllers. She keeps a low profile, with no executive title in recent filings. The email is the board-secretary IR contact from company filings.

name: Jiang Ling
current_role: Chairman, Zhejiang Sling Intelligent Drive Group (斯菱智驱, formerly Zhejiang Sling Automobile Bearing; SZSE 301550)
profile: Jiang Ling (姜岭, born 1973) founded and, with his daughter Jiang Nan, controls Sling, an aftermarket auto-bearing maker in Xinchang, Zhejiang. After its 2023 ChiNext listing, the company moved into humanoid-robot joint parts such as harmonic reducers, and in 2026 it renamed itself 'Sling Intelligent Drive'.
interesting_fact: Sling built a dedicated R&D team in 2023 for humanoid and collaborative-robot joint components. By end-2024 it had its first harmonic-reducer production line running, a pivot from car bearings into robotics.
deep_cut_fact: He started at the very bottom of the industry: from August 1990, aged 17, he worked as a factory worker at the Zhejiang Xinchang Bearing General Factory for a decade. In 2000 he became general manager of Xinchang Sanhe Bearing, and he later built Sling.
notes: 'Jiang Nan' (shared_with) is his daughter and co-controller, per the filings. The robotics pivot makes this a good fit for an automation or hardware story. He keeps a low profile, so the best route is the company's securities office (stock@bbsbearing.com).

name: Xiao Chunming
current_role: Unclear. Possibly the founder of Guizhou Honglicheng (宏立城) Group, Guiyang, whose founder is reported as 肖春红 (Xiao Chunhong)
profile: Listed by Hurun (2012-2015) for Honglicheng real estate. Guizhou Honglicheng Group is the Guiyang developer behind the giant Huaguoyuan (花果园) complex, but Chinese media name its founder as 肖春红 (Xiao Chunhong), not 肖春明. This may be the same person under a variant name, though that could not be confirmed.
interesting_fact: Honglicheng's Huaguoyuan project in Guiyang was nicknamed 'China's No.1 mega-development' (中国第一神盘) for its enormous scale.
notes: Name mismatch: no source links '肖春明' to Honglicheng, while the reported founder is 肖春红, so verify identity before any outreach. Media since 2022 report that the group is under heavy financial strain (court enforcement actions and a troubled Indonesian new-town project, 美加达新城). He has been off the rich lists since 2015, making him a weak candidate. No published contacts found.

name: Huang Wen Tsai
current_role: Chairman, Star River Group (星河湾集团), Guangzhou
profile: Huang Wenzai (黄文仔) founded a lumber business in Guangzhou in 1995, the predecessor of Star River, and built it into a luxury residential developer known for its high-spec 'Star River' communities. As of 2026 he is personally leading Star River's bid for the roughly 40-billion-yuan Shaxi village redevelopment in Panyu, Guangzhou's largest urban-renewal project.
interesting_fact: Star River started out as a timber trading company before turning into one of China's best-known luxury home brands. The group employs around 10,000 people.
notes: Off the Forbes list since 2022. In August 2026 he was reported to be frequently on site in Shaxi village himself to push the redevelopment (https://www.36kr.com/p/3923129393180037). He is very private, and no verified official website or press contact was found (starriver.com.cn is a parked domain). The route would be via Star River Group's Guangzhou headquarters.

name: Peter Livanos
current_role: Chairman, GasLog Ltd (LNG shipping) and head of the family-owned Ceres Shipping / Ceres Hellenic Shipping Enterprises
profile: Greek shipowner (born 1958), son of shipping magnate George P. Livanos and grandson of Yiannis Carras. He took over Ceres after his father's death in 1997, steered the group into LNG carriers around 2000 and founded GasLog in 2003. GasLog was later NYSE-listed and was taken private in 2021 with BlackRock's GIP. He remains its chairman.
interesting_fact: He was once a majority shareholder of Aston Martin, before Ford took control of the British carmaker. He is also known as a keen competitive yachtsman.
deep_cut_fact: He is an engineer by training, with a B.S. from Columbia University's engineering school (1981) after the Buckley School and Le Rosey. The Massachusetts Maritime Academy awarded him an honorary Doctorate of Science.
notes: A strong fit for an energy podcast, as an LNG shipping pioneer who has spoken publicly on LNG's future (Marine Money, see https://www.freightwaves.com/news/shipping-titan-peter-livanos-lays-out-his-vision-for-lngs-future). He is otherwise very private. Input data is sparse (Forbes 1997 only), but the identity is clear. The best route is GasLog's corporate contact.

name: Liu Ce
current_role: Director and Deputy General Manager, Changyu Holding Group (长裕集团, SSE 603407, Zibo, Shandong); chairman of subsidiaries Dikaikai New Materials and Dikaikai Environmental
profile: Liu Ce (刘策, born 1984, master's degree) and his father Liu Qiyong (刘其永, the chairman) are the actual controllers of Changyu Holding Group, with about 53% between them. Changyu makes zirconium chemicals, specialty nylon and fine chemicals in Zibo. It listed on the Shanghai main board in May 2026, which put the family on the Hurun list.
interesting_fact: Changyu says it has the world's largest production capacity for zirconium oxychloride, the feedstock for zirconia ceramics and other advanced zirconium materials.
deep_cut_fact: Despite being the founder's son, he started on the factory floor: in 2011 he worked as a production worker at Guangyin New Materials, then as a technician at Zibo Guangcheng Chemical. He later set up the Dikaikai New Materials business from scratch in 2013-14 and ran it as general manager.
notes: The input's 'Liu Qiyong' is written 刘其永 in filings and is his father and co-controller. A new listing (May 2026), with the next generation taking over day to day. The IR office is the board office (contact person Li Yaqun), reachable at ir@changyuintl.com.

name: Wang Zhenghua
current_role: Founder and co-controller (with son Wang Yu) of Spring Airlines (SSE 601021) via parent Shanghai Spring International Travel Service; director and largest individual shareholder
profile: Former Shanghai district official who quit public service around age 40 and founded Spring Travel Agency in 1981, one of China's first private travel agencies. In 2004-05 he launched Spring Airlines, mainland China's first low-cost carrier and later its only listed private airline. Spring is now a fleet of about 120 Airbus A320s. His son Wang Yu now jointly controls the group.
interesting_fact: He is famously frugal: 'When we go to the conferences in London and Singapore, we take the bus or subway, not taxis.' Spring staff abroad shared cheap hotel rooms and cooked their own meals.
deep_cut_fact: He started Spring Travel with just 1,000 yuan of capital. In the 2008 crisis, while rivals cut back, he made the largest investment in the company's history: a final payment on its first aircraft and deposits on eight new A320s, funded by a first loan from Germany's HSH Nordbank.
notes: Now in his 80s (China Daily gave his age as 70 in 2013). The 2025 annual report (April 2026) still lists him as co-controller with son Wang Yu, who succeeded him in the day-to-day leadership. A legendary entrepreneur story. The best route is via the Spring Airlines board office (ir@ch.com).

name: Jalaj Ashwin Dani
current_role: Co-promoter, Asian Paints; Chairman of the Board, IIM Tiruchirappalli; Chairperson, Dani Foundation
profile: Third-generation member of the Dani family, a founding family of Asian Paints, India's largest paint company. He previously held senior roles there covering international business and supply chain. He now invests via Asiana AIF and direct deals in tech, healthcare, manufacturing and consumer, and runs large-scale philanthropy.
interesting_fact: He helped pioneer new sports ventures in India, including the Ultimate Table Tennis league and the Indian Super League club Chennaiyin FC. Through the Dani Sports Foundation and the 'Sportscom' movement, he campaigns for grassroots sport and physical literacy.
deep_cut_fact: He credits his grandfather Suryakant Dani, an Asian Paints co-founder, with his collaborative model of giving, and follows 'Gupt Daan', the tradition of giving privately without seeking credit. Working with the ELMS Sports Foundation, his family's foundations have helped train more than 20,000 physical-education teachers in India.
notes: Sports-ecosystem and impact-investing work is the best podcast hook. The contact form and social accounts belong to the Dani Sports Foundation, not to him personally. The Asian Paints IR email is a poor route for a personal invitation. His wife Vita founded Ultimate Table Tennis and co-owns Chennaiyin FC.

name: Gao Yi
current_role: Founder, chairman and actual controller, Yifeng Pharmacy Chain (益丰药房, SSE 603939), Changsha
profile: Gao Yi (高毅, born 1968, Changde, Hunan; MBA) entered drug distribution in the 1990s and founded Yifeng Pharmacy in 2001. Yifeng became Hunan's first listed pharmacy chain in 2015 and now has well over 10,000 stores, including franchised ones, with 2025 revenue of about 24.4 billion yuan. He is also a former Hunan provincial People's Congress deputy.
interesting_fact: During the 2008 financial crisis, he raised 200 million yuan for Yifeng against the market. Chinese profiles say this broke the investment banks' habit of backing only the top five pharmacy chains.
deep_cut_fact: Before Yifeng, he restructured Hunan Deyuan Pharmaceutical in Changde, a deal remembered locally as the 'child absorbing the parent' (子并母). His motto: 'Only if you give ordinary people benefits will they give benefits back to you.'
notes: The deep-cut and interesting facts come from a Chinese brand-profile aggregator (CNPP), so treat them as moderately reliable. He gives occasional interviews on franchising and digitalisation in pharmacy retail. The best route is the board office (ir@yfdyf.com).

name: Jörg-Uwe Goldbeck
current_role: Co-CEO / managing director, GOLDBECK GmbH (Bielefeld); board member, Ortwin Goldbeck Holding SE
profile: Son of Ortwin Goldbeck, who founded the company in 1969 with seven employees. He and his brother Jan-Hendrik took over in 2007 and run Goldbeck as co-leaders. It is one of Germany's largest builders, using systemised, prefabricated construction for factories, warehouses, offices, schools, car parks and housing.
interesting_fact: Goldbeck was one of the main builders of Tesla's Gigafactory near Berlin. The company treats buildings like industrial products: it designs and makes major components in-house, erects them and can operate them afterwards.
deep_cut_fact: His one-line summary of the company's philosophy, from a 2021 Porsche Consulting interview: 'We don't build anything we don't plan, and we don't plan anything we don't build.' He also said: 'We've always done things differently.'
notes: His brother Jan-Hendrik is the more public face (OMR podcast, 2026). Goldbeck's industrial work, including the Tesla factory, links naturally to energy and data-centre topics. The press email comes from a 2019 release, so confirm it is current; the published main line is +49 521 94 880.

name: Eduard Shifrin
current_role: London-based author and creator of the 'Kabbalah of Information'; co-founder of Midland Group (former owner of Zaporizhstal)
profile: Metallurgical engineer (PhD 1992), born in Dnipropetrovsk in 1960. With Alex Shnaider he co-founded Midland Group, which owned Ukraine's Zaporizhstal steelworks, Maccabi Tel Aviv and the Midland F1 team. Zaporizhstal was sold in 2010. He now lives in London and writes books, newspaper columns and music.
interesting_fact: He co-owned a Formula One team (Midland F1 Racing). Today he writes and records jazz-rock-blues songs released as 'Shyfrin Alliance', recorded in Paris.
deep_cut_fact: As a schoolboy in 1976-77 he won first place in the National Ukrainian Physics Olympiad. He started his career in 1983 as an assistant foreman at the Dniprospetsstal steel plant in Zaporizhzhia. His children's book 'Travels with Sushi in the Land of the Mind' was named a 2020 Independent Press Award Distinguished Favorite.
notes: He now uses the spelling 'Shyfrin'. Steel is in the past, so the best hooks are his books (e.g. 'From Infinity to Man', 2019; 'The Relativity of Death', 2026), his Jerusalem Post Kabbalah column and his sponsorship of Jewish Book Week in London. The Times of Israel blog has a 'Contact Me' form. The Wikipedia article is flagged as promotional, so cross-check details.

name: Rao Wei
current_role: Chairman (and legal representative), Shenzhen New Industries Biomedical Engineering (Snibe, 新产业, SZSE 300832)
profile: Rao Wei (饶微) joined Snibe in 1997, aged 33, when it was an 18-person trading firm. He led its move into in-house chemiluminescence immunoassay analysers and reagents, and it is now China's leading domestic player in that field, listed in Shenzhen in 2020. He is a major holder but not the founder or controller.
interesting_fact: Snibe's chemiluminescence R&D, started in 2000, took about a decade to pay off. During that time Rao and another major shareholder gave up dividends to reinvest everything in R&D, and spent over 100 million yuan learning to make reagent raw materials in-house.
deep_cut_fact: The trigger was a setback: soon after he joined, a Swiss supplier pulled Snibe's distribution rights, which convinced him China needed its own core technology. The first lab was set up in a residential flat in Nanshan, Shenzhen. Today the campus is planted with slow-growing golden nanmu and huanghuali trees, a nod to his goal of a 'century-old company' benchmarked on Roche.
notes: A technology-first, 'self-reliance' story that suits an entrepreneurship podcast. He gave a long interview to China Securities Journal in 2023. The IR email comes from the 2020 annual report summary, so confirm it is still current. In 2012 he insisted that about 120 employees hold shares directly as individuals.

name: Arthur Levine
current_role: Founding Partner and Co-Chairperson of the Executive Committee, Levine Leichtman Capital Partners (LLCP), Beverly Hills; co-owner of NWSL's San Diego Wave FC
profile: Arthur Levine co-founded Levine Leichtman Capital Partners in 1984 with his wife Lauren Leichtman, whom he married in 1979. Before that he invested in and was president of the radio syndicator Westwood One. LLCP is a middle-market 'structured private equity' firm that has raised about $14.8bn across 15 funds. Its exits include Tropical Smoothie Cafe, Wetzel's Pretzels and Nothing Bundt Cakes.
interesting_fact: In 2024 he and Leichtman bought the NWSL's San Diego Wave FC for about $113 million, then a record for a women's soccer club.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as a lawyer and business manager, not a financier: he holds a J.D. from Columbia Law School, where he was a Harlan Fiske Stone Scholar, and an MBA from UCLA Anderson.
notes: His wife and co-founder Lauren Leichtman is the more public face, especially for the San Diego Wave, where she is the NWSL governor. The best route is LLCP's Beverly Hills main office or its media page. The Wave sale was announced in March 2024 (Loeb), and Forbes dates the purchase to October 2024.

name: Sarah Humphreys Atkins
current_role: President, J.P. Humphreys Foundation; director, TAMKO Building Products; board member, Moving Picture Institute; trustee, Capital Research Center
profile: Heiress to the TAMKO roofing fortune and only granddaughter of founder E.L. Craig. TAMKO is the fourth-largest US shingle maker, with about $1.2bn in revenue in 2023. Carlyle bought 25% in 2019, and she and her brother David (CEO) split the rest with their families. She sits on TAMKO's board with her husband Paul Atkins, chairman of the SEC, and leads the family's J.P. Humphreys Foundation.
interesting_fact: Her grandfather E.L. Craig founded TAMKO in 1944 at the age of 69, in an old streetcar barn in Joplin, Missouri.
deep_cut_fact: She is a long-time builder of free-market nonprofits. She has served on the boards of the Foundation for Economic Education, Free to Choose Network, Atlas Network and The Future of Freedom Foundation, and now sits on the board of the Moving Picture Institute, which backs liberty-themed films.
notes: Very private, with no personal social media found. Her husband is the sitting SEC chairman, so expect sensitivity around any outreach that touches on markets or regulation. The TAMKO communications office is the company's media contact, not hers personally. The nonprofit boards (Capital Research Center, Moving Picture Institute) are an alternative route.
